Fix attributed to c0676c7ca (PR #4375), confirmed in v1.7.2207 and absent from v1.6.2112 by git merge-base; the window holds 248 commits, 3 touching DxilDbgValueToDbgDeclare.cpp, so attribution is strong, not proven.

**[#3414](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/3414) — DXIL Modifying recursive payload does not work**  
<sub>batch 012 · triaged against `13730886e` · drafted by `claude-opus-4.6 (GitHub Copilot CLI)` · reviewed by `Claude Sonnet independent review (batch-012 step-10; blind 3414)`</sub>

Fixed. From v1.6.2104 to v1.8.2502 (13 consecutive stable releases) DXC passed a closest-hit shader's own inout payload object straight to dx.op.traceRay instead of a copy, eliding the copy-in/copy-out that inout requires; on the same broken binary the reporter's workaround variant gets a distinct temporary. Clean on v1.4.1907 and v1.5.2010 and on every release from v1.8.2505 onward. Likely fixed by 053e7ac65 (PR #7440), which moves UDT intrinsic arg copy-in/copy-out ahead of SROA and adds a test for a payload passed as a pointer parameter - strong but not certain, 162-commit window. Nothing was executed on a GPU.

**[#3954](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/3954) — AnyHit Shader hits `llvm_unreachable("Unexpected matrix subscript use.")`**  
<sub>batch 014 · triaged against `13730886e` · drafted by `claude-opus-4.6 (GitHub Copilot CLI)` · reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol (independent draft review, step 10)`</sub>

Does not reproduce on main (1.9.0.5433, 13730886e): the AnyHit repro compiles clean at -T lib_6_3, the oldest profile that can express [shader(anyhit)]. Reproduced on all 14 stable releases from v1.4.1907 through v1.8.2407 and clean from v1.8.2502 on, with no invalid probes, so the defect predates the oldest release carrying a dxc asset. Scored with internal_failure, which is load-bearing: the same defect exits 0xC0000005 with completely empty stderr (v1.4.1907, v1.5.2010), 0xE0000002 'Internal compiler error: LLVM Unreachable' (v1.6.2104), 0x80AA001C with the reporter's message (v1.6.2106, v1.6.2112), and E_FAIL with 'error: Unexpected matrix subscript use.' (v1.7.2207..v1.8.2407, classified only by the UNREACHABLE marker since E_FAIL is excluded from INTERNAL_STATUS); manual-case-predicate-counterfactual.txt measures three naive predicates each reporting a different wrong history. Cause: HLMatrixSubscriptUseReplacer::replaceUses handles only loads and stores, and pre-fix codegen left .r an lvalue so it emitted 'bitcast float* to <1 x float>*' on the subscript pointer; v1.8.2502 loads the <3 x float> and extractelements instead, so the fix is in Sema/codegen, not the lowering pass. Strong but unbisected attribution to 0372fb792 (PR #6930), which adds CK_LValueToRValue in LookupVectorMemberExprForHLSL for duplicate-element swizzles: present in v1.8.2502, absent from v1.8.2407, and on v1.8.2407 .r.x compiles while .r.xx crashes; the tag window is 133 commits, 4 touching SemaHLSL.cpp, and nothing was built at that commit. The fix emits correct code rather than silence -- the repro and the reporter's .xxx workaround produce byte-identical DXIL on v1.8.2502 and on main. The reporter's quoted output matches v1.6.2106 and v1.6.2112 exactly, line 91 included. Not raytracing-specific: the identical subscript in cs_6_0 fails the same way on v1.4.1907, v1.6.2106 and v1.8.2407. Controls (workaround, feature-presence anyhit, compute stage, duplicate and no-duplicate swizzle) were run on 4-5 representative builds, not all 20.

*History:* fixed in v1.8.2502 (repro'd v1.4.1907..v1.8.2407, 14 releases; clean v1.8.2502..v1.9.2607, 6 releases; no invalid probes; defect predates the oldest release carrying a dxc asset)

*Labels:* add `matrix-bug`.

A captured repeated-run set reproduced STATUS_HEAP_CORRUPTION (0xC0000374) in 33/40 v1.6.2104 runs and 28/40 v1.6.2106 runs; v1.5.2010 and v1.6.2112 were each clean in 30/30, and later release probes were clean through v1.9.2607. The v1.9.2607 release binary and current main Debug were each clean in 55/55 runs across ps_6_0 and cs_6_0, with expected SPIR-V inspected on main. The original -fcgl -Vd flags avoided a separate SPIRV-Tools crash fixed by PR #4280; all four flag combinations repeatedly reproduce on both affected releases, so the flags do not suppress this crash. Application Verifier/page heap was not rerun.

**[#8732](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/8732) — [SPIR-V] SPV_EXT_descriptor_heap mixed bound/heap aliasing causes silent miscompilation or ICE**  
<sub>batch 005 · triaged against `13730886e` · drafted by `claude-opus-4.5 (GitHub Copilot CLI)` · reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol (independent draft review, step 10)`</sub>

Filed against the unmerged branch of PR #8517; the VarDecl alias map it blames does not exist on main (zero occurrences of descriptorHeapImageAliasVars, createDescriptorHeapIndexVar, diagnoseDescriptorHeapAliasMixing et al). On main at 13730886e all five cases fail loudly instead of silently: defects 1-3 and the still-undiagnosed heap-only conditional die on 'generated SPIR-V is invalid: [VUID-StandaloneSpirv-OpTypeImage-06924] Cannot store to OpTypeImage', defect 4 on 'UAV support not implemented with non-emulated heaps'. Re-run with -Vd the module is semantically correct -- both descriptors store into one Function image variable, last store wins, %boundTex preserved -- so main is illegal, not wrong; Interlocked* on a heap-loaded texture is simply unsupported there (a heap-only control with no bound resource fails identically). v1.9.2607 matches main exactly. Separately, the reporter's documented workaround (separate variables) compiles on v1.9.2607 but now fails on main with the UniformConstant ArrayStride rule newly enforced by the SPIRV-Tools 1c336172 bump (ec2ba18da), tracked as #8740 -- so every shader here that actually indexes ResourceDescriptorHeap fails validation on main today, though a control that sets -fspv-use-descriptor-heap without indexing the heap still compiles.

> ⚠️ **Issue text is stale.** Title says 'silent miscompilation or ICE', but the body's own Actual Behavior section says all four filed defects are now diagnosed at compile time and defect 4 no longer ICEs -- only the heap-only conditional case is still described as silent. Neither state is reachable from main: the issue is filed against the unmerged branch of PR #8517 and says so only in passing, so anyone checking it against main or any release sees a loud validation error and concludes it cannot be reproduced.

*History:* unmeasurable -- only v1.9.2607 of the 20 releases in the bisection sequence can run the repro; the other 19 answer Unknown argument: '-fspv-use-descriptor-heap'. NOT never-repro'd-in-releases and not a fix.

*Labels:* add `correctness`.

**[#3005](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/3005) — Generated separate PDB files have possibly invalid header**  
<sub>batch 007 · triaged against `13730886e` · drafted by `GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.79-2 (model not self-identifiable)` · reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol (independent draft review, step 10)`</sub>

Still reproduces on main (13730886e). The separate PDB written by -Fd declares NumBlocks one block short, so the file's own stream directory addresses a block the superblock says does not exist; cause is NumBlockAddrBlocks being written but never counted at lib/DXIL/DxilPDB.cpp:132. Present in all 21 builds measured. LLVM and llvm-pdbutil accept the file; Microsoft's reference MSF implementation would refuse to read the last page. The actionable finding is that PR #5767 (Fixes #3005, by a maintainer, reviewed and format-clean in Nov 2023) was closed unmerged by an inactivity sweep on 2026-01-22.

> ⚠️ **Issue text is stale.** A maintainer comment left standing: @damyanp asked on 2024-06-27 'it looks like you have a PR prepared for this. How far off is that from being ready to go in?' It was never answered, and the PR it refers to (#5767) was closed unmerged on 2026-01-22, so the thread reads top-down as though a fix is pending when none is. Title and body are still accurate -- the hex dump reproduces exactly on v1.5.2010.

*History:* always-repro'd across v1.4.1907..v1.9.2607 (all 20 releases) plus main-debug -- established by reading the PDB's bytes on all 21 builds (manual-case-msf-header-history.txt), NOT by the predicate. Do not read the bisect line as symptom history: it reports v1.4.1907 no-repro because that release's -dumpbin cannot read a PDB and the precondition predicate fails, not because the defect is absent -- v1.4.1907 writes the identical short NumBlocks. Source dating puts introduction at 2dec1cd0d (2019-05-29), before the oldest probeable release.

**[#3305](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/3305) — Empty Payload struct not recognized in DXIL**  
<sub>batch 007 · triaged against `13730886e` · drafted by `claude-sonnet-4.6 (GitHub Copilot CLI)` · reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol (independent draft review, step 10)`</sub>

DXIL still rejects an empty payload struct while SPIR-V compiles it, unchanged on every measurable build (v1.4.1907..v1.9.2607 and main). The DXIL diagnostic misnames its cause: it says the shader must include an inout payload structure parameter, but the parameter is present and what CGHLSLMS.cpp:2492 checks is payloadSizeInBytes == 0 -- a payload whose only member is an empty struct gets the same message, and since PR #5131 (2023-04) a genuinely missing parameter gets an accurate Sema message instead. Whether an empty payload should be legal is a language/product decision, deliberate since 2018 and still unanswered on the thread; the wrong message is separately fixable either way.

*History:* always-repro'd across v1.4.1907..v1.9.2607 (all 20 releases probed linearly, no invalid probes); the SPIR-V half of the same captures compiles in 19 of 20, v1.5.2010 onward -- only v1.4.1907 lacks SPIR-V codegen. Predates the 2020-12 report

*Labels:* add `diagnostic`.

**[#4096](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/4096) — `bool` cast operator doesn't implicitly trigger**  
<sub>batch 012 · triaged against `13730886e` · drafted by `claude-sonnet-4.5 (GitHub Copilot CLI)` · reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol (independent draft review, step 10)`</sub>

Reported symptom present on all 16 stable releases that can compile the input (v1.6.2112 2021-12-08 .. v1.9.2607) and on main; the 4 older releases answer 'Unknown HLSL version: 2021' and are invalid probes, confirmed per release with a minimal -HV 2021 presence control. Filed 2021-11-22, 16 days before v1.6.2112, so no stable release covers the reporter's own build. The operator body has never executed: with the operator and the flat conversion made to disagree, all 15 releases v1.6.2112..v1.9.2602.24 emit i32 111 (flat conversion), never 222. SHAPE CHANGE at v1.9.2607: PR #8206 / commit b13e386be (2026-04-14) added err_hlsl_unsupported_conversion_operator, so main now rejects the DECLARATION as well as the if - the only commit touching SemaDeclCXX.cpp in that 224-commit window. Not a fix; the construct fails earlier. Root cause named in the 2023-02-08 comment is unchanged: SemaOverload.cpp:1136 disables TryUserDefinedConversion for HLSL. Clang (hlsl_clang_trunk) DOES invoke operator bool() in an if condition - stores 222 - with controls ruling out the resource and the shader shape; for an explicit (bool)A cast Clang still flat-converts. Design position may already be on record: milestoned HLSL 202x, and llvm-beanz on hlsl-specs PR #37 (discussion_r1158553249, 2023-04-05, cross-referenced here 2023-04-06) said new operator overloads will be 202x features gated on the 202x overload-resolution rework (hlsl-specs #34). Where the work belongs is therefore a product/language decision, not a triage conclusion.

*History:* always-repro'd across v1.6.2112..v1.9.2607 (16 releases, linear scan); 4 older releases predate HLSL 2021 and are invalid probes

*Labels:* add `type-system`, `enhancement`.

**[#4710](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/4710) — Incorrectly erroring with error: Index for resource array inside cbuffer must be a literal expression**  
<sub>batch 017 · triaged against `13730886e` · drafted by `claude-opus-5` · reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol`</sub>

Reproduces on main and is a regression: v1.4.1907 compiles the reporter's shader and emits correct DXIL (handles t0/t5/t10/t15, cbuffer regIndex 0/9/18/27); v1.5.2010 is the first release to reject it and all 19 later releases do too. 20 stable releases scanned with 3 positive controls per binary (63 assertions, 0 failures) because the symptom is a diagnostic and the invalid-probe net cannot see it. The guard is HLModule::GetBindingForResourceInCB (lib/HLSL/HLModule.cpp:816, !hasAllConstantIndices), reached from DxilGenerationPass -- confirmed by a cdb stack -- and dxc -Odump shows -dxilgen at index 36 runs before -dxil-loop-unroll at 41, so [unroll] cannot make the index literal in time. Attributed to 94460c988 'Support register binding on resource in cbuffer (#2582)' (in v1.5.2010, not v1.4.1907; 434-commit window), which introduced per-element register binding and rewrote resource-in-cb4.hlsl from a passing binding table to a CHECK for this error. FXC ps_5_0 on CE produces the same bindings as old DXC, measuring the fxc-disagrees label for the first time; FXC ps_5_1 fails, as the reporter said. Whether the restriction is intended is a design question this triage does not settle.

*Labels:* add `bug`, `diagnostic`, `check-in-clang`.

**[#4763](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/4763) — DXC doesn't report an error when placing a resource in a ConstantBuffer**  
<sub>batch 017 · triaged against `13730886e` · drafted by `claude-opus-5` · reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol`</sub>

Both halves of the report still reproduce on main (1.10 5433-ab540090, 13730886e) and on all 20 stable releases v1.4.1907..v1.9.2607: the repro compiles with exit 0 and zero diagnostics while three resource types sit in cbuffers, and the reporter's 2022 offset/size table is still numerically exact (myInt at 12 with size 16 after StructuredBuffer<float3>, at 64 with size 68 after StructuredBuffer<float4x4>). dxv reports Validation succeeded, so this is silent acceptance rather than a front-end gap the validator catches. Not an oversight: commit 2b4f3e480 (2017) deliberately narrowed the pre-existing 'object types not supported' error to cbuffer/tbuffer view ARRAYS and declared resources zero-size; the array form is still diagnosed on every release probed (positive control, E_FAIL, one diagnostic), and in-tree tests assert the scalar form keeps working, so whether an error is owed is a language decision -- hlsl-specs#225 names this issue as needing it. FXC is silent too, but lays every cbuffer out as size 4 at offset 0, so the same source yields two host-visible layouts with no diagnostic from either compiler. The layout half has a mechanical cause: CGHLSLMS.cpp:1282 applies the zero-size rule only when !IsHLSLStructuredBufferType(Ty), so a StructuredBuffer<T> member is charged sizeof(T). Buffer<T> had the identical bug and was fixed by that same line (e6ba792e2, 2021-05-26), measured here as changing between v1.6.2104 and v1.6.2106.

*Labels:* add `bug`, `correctness`, `diagnostic`.

**[#4307](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/4307) — Have a more explicit error when trying to use a struct member output interpolator as an input**  
<sub>batch 015 · triaged against `13730886e` · drafted by `claude-opus-5` · reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol (independent draft review, step 10)`</sub>

Reproduces verbatim on main (13730886e) and on every release with mesh shaders: v1.5.2010 at ms_6_5 and all 18 releases v1.6.2104-v1.9.2607 at ms_6_6 emit `repro.hlsl:11: error: Function main with parameter is not permitted, it should be inlined.` (v1.4.1907 has no mesh shaders; control-confirmed, not fixed). /Od is not load-bearing. Decisive finding: DXC already has the diagnostic being asked for. Reading the whole element instead of one member gives `case-elem-read.hlsl:22:18: error: output arrays of a mesh shader can not be read from` with a caret - the right message on the right line - on 18/18 mesh-capable releases. That is err_hlsl_load_from_mesh_out_arrays (DiagnosticSemaKinds.td:7888), emitted at SemaExpr.cpp:698 under `isa<ArraySubscriptExpr>(E) && IsExprAccessingMeshOutArray(E)`; `_vertices[i].m_value` is a MemberExpr, and IsExprAccessingMeshOutArray (SemaExpr.cpp:613) has no MemberExpr case either, so Sema is silent (-fcgl exits 0). The read-modify-write then reaches LegalizeDxilInputOutputs, whose bLoad&&bStore switch has no case for the mesh quals and falls through without a temp (ScalarReplAggregatesHLSL.cpp:6065), so the entry point keeps its parameter and the DXIL validator emits the generic Flow.FunctionCall message located on the signature. Fix shape: extend an existing check to arr[i].member, not write a new diagnostic; diagnostic and guard both date to 968fe4113 (2019-07-11), so nothing regressed. Separately, a Debug build ASSERTS on the same repro (DXASSERT(0, \"invalid input qual here\"), exit 0x80000003) before the reported message - a defect in its own right, hence the crash label despite enhancement-not-bug. The body last paragraph does not reproduce: the member passed to an `out float` param compiles CLEAN on main and all 18 releases, the whole element passed to `out Vertex` gets the good diagnostic, and only `inout` reproduces.

> ⚠️ **Issue text is stale.** Body's last paragraph (the same error appears when the member is passed to a function parameter 'even if the parameter of the function is marked as out') does not describe any tested compiler: member -> out float compiles cleanly on main and all 18 mesh-capable releases; whole element -> out Vertex produces the good Sema diagnostic; only inout reproduces the vague validation error. Stated neutrally - the variants are derived mechanically from the reporter's own shader but are not their original code, and the report is from 2022.

*Labels:* add `enhancement`, `incorrect-code`, `crash`.

**[#4708](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/4708) — Free operator overload**  
<sub>batch 017 · triaged against `13730886e` · drafted by `claude-opus-5` · reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol`</sub>

Feature request, not a defect: HLSL has never supported non-member (free) operator overloading, and DXC's rejection is deliberate and asserted in-tree (SemaHLSL/v2021/operators/global-overload-disallowed.hlsl). hlsl-specs proposal 0008 was Accepted in July 2025 targeting HLSL 202y. Clang trunk already compiles the reporter's shader unmodified and folds 2.0+2.0 through the free operator to float 4.000000e+00. Free operator rejected on all 16 of 20 releases that can express the repro; the 4 oldest are unmeasurable (no HLSL 2021 templates), not clean. Member-operator and renamed-free-function controls compile everywhere, isolating the restriction to free operators. v1.8.2403 added a declaration-site diagnostic (PR #5796) - a diagnostic improvement, not a regression.

> ⚠️ **Issue text is stale.** Standing maintainer comment (2023-06-30) names HLSL 202x; hlsl-specs proposal 0008 was retargeted to 202y (2025-04-01) and marked Accepted (2025-07-22). Version number only; the comment's substance was correct.

*Labels:* add `enhancement`.

**[#4619](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/4619) — How to get thread group size and output primitive topology in MeshShader?**  
<sub>batch 016 · triaged against `13730886e` · drafted by `claude-opus-5` · reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol`</sub>

Two asks with opposite answers, and the finding is what happened to the resolution rather than the repro. (A) GetThreadGroupSize returning 0,0,0 for mesh shaders was a real bug, fixed 2022-10-27 by PR #4745 -- two months after this issue was filed, by a PR that never referenced it. closingIssuesReferences is empty, the timeline has no cross-reference of any kind, and the issue still has 0 comments; it was then labelled enhancement+reflection in 2024-01 (15 months after the fix shipped) and milestoned Backlog in 2024-09, both against a state that was already obsolete. On main (13730886e) it returns the declared 32,2,1. (B) Output primitive topology still has no accessor on ID3D12ShaderReflection, on any of 20 releases or on main: GSOutputTopology comes from DxilModule::GetStreamPrimitiveTopology(), only ever set for GS, and D3D12_SHADER_DESC has no mesh member, so this needs new API surface -- enhancement, matching the existing label, now measured rather than assumed. The data is in the container, so there is a workaround today: PSVRuntimeInfo1::MS1.MeshOutputTopology (=2 Triangle) and the DXIL mesh entry-point tag 9, field 3. Measured with a host harness (refl4619.cpp) registered as a compiler, because dxc.exe never calls the interface and dxa -dumpreflection cannot answer either half -- D3DReflectionDumper has zero GetThreadGroupSize call sites and prints GSOutputTopology only for geometry shaders. 5 controls (compute, amplification, pixel, geometry, mesh-line) all pass --expect no-match.

> ⚠️ **Issue text is stale.** The body's first sentence -- 'I tried ID3D12ShaderReflection::GetThreadGroupSize, but got 0, 0, 0 all the time' -- has been false of every DXC since v1.7.2212 (2022-12-16). It was true when filed (v1.7.2207 reproduces), so this is staleness by the compiler moving, not by bad reporting. The harm is the usual one inverted: a reader spot-checking the issue finds GetThreadGroupSize works and may close the whole thing, dropping the still-open topology half; a reader who trusts the text instead goes looking for a bug fixed four years ago. The title names both asks and so overstates the remaining work. Nothing in the thread records the fix.

**[#2128](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/2128) — Generated bytecode by dxc has very higher compression ratio**  
<sub>batch 006 · triaged against `13730886e` · drafted by `claude-opus-4.6 (Copilot CLI)` · reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol`</sub>

Confirmed and unchanged since v1.4.1907. dxc objects zip to 3.7x fxc's for the same shaders (fxc ratio 0.33 vs reporter's ~0.30; dxc -Qstrip_reflect 0.77 vs reporter's 0.80-0.85); raw sizes differ by 1.5%, so the whole gap is compressibility. The DXIL part alone deflates to 0.848/0.900 -- LLVM 3.7 bitcode is bit-packed and near entropy-dense where DXBC's SHEX is byte-aligned repetitive tokens (0.271). Half of BitMD's 2019 comment landed: reflection moved out of the module into STAT between v1.4.1907 and v1.5.2010, cutting corpus size 39% raw, but the bitcode's compressibility never moved (0.839 -> 0.851 -> 0.848). Division's 2022 question answered: PC dxc has no shader-object compression to disable -- zlib is used only by the PDB writer and the SRCI source part. Not a defect; a container-encoding decision.

*Labels:* add `fxc-disagrees`, `enhancement`.

*No Compiler Explorer link:* The symptom is the byte size and deflate ratio of the compiled object. Compiler Explorer panes show text disassembly; no pane can show an object's byte count, and none can run deflate. A link would show fxc, dxc and clang all succeeding, which published bare reads as 'cannot reproduce' -- the #2191 trap, and here without even #2191's partial value (there is no release-vs-debug distinction to demonstrate). A Clang pane was considered and rejected for the same reason: clang's HLSL path emits the same LLVM bitcode encoding, so it inherits the property by construction, but a text pane still cannot display it -- the claim would be asserted, not shown. The shareable repro is measure.py, committed in this directory, which recompiles the corpus and prints bytes/deflated/ratio; manual-case-compression.txt is its verified output.

**[#2604](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/2604) — Handle -Fc in Compile API**  
<sub>batch 010 · triaged against `13730886e` · drafted by `GitHub Copilot CLI (claude-opus-4.6)` · reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol (SKILL.md step 10 initial and final-draft reviews, applied selectively at collation)`</sub>

Unimplemented, exactly as filed. -Fc is Flags<[DriverOption]> only (HLSLOptions.td:505); dxc.exe parses with DxcFlags = CoreOption\|DriverOption (dxclib/dxc.cpp:1437) while the library parses with CompilerFlags = CoreOption alone (dxcompiler/dxcutil.cpp:114), so in the API path -Fc becomes OPT_UNKNOWN and ReadDxcOpts fails the parse (HLSLOptions.cpp:534-537); dxcutil::ReadOptsAndValidate builds a finished DxcResult carrying E_INVALIDARG and both entry points return S_OK with it (dxcompilerobj.cpp:562-566, :1908-1911). Measured with a committed C++ harness (fc2604.cpp) against dxcompiler.dll: 10 cases, both interfaces, DXIL and SPIR-V, 21 releases + main -- identical throughout. IMPORTANT for a prospective PR: adding CoreOption to -Fc is NOT the fix. opts.AssemblyCode has no reader anywhere under tools/clang/tools/dxcompiler/ (git grep exits 1 there, 10 hits repo-wide), and no Compile path produces DXC_OUT_DISASSEMBLY -- the only producer is Disassemble (dxcompilerobj.cpp:1386), as dxcapi.h:381 documents. That patch would convert a loud failure into a silent one. Separable finding: docs/SPIR-V.rst:4197-4198 claims the listed options are also recognized by the library API calls, and :4211 lists -Fc; measured false on every release, including with -spirv. That doc text (8702f97df 2017, 474954a6e 2018) predates the issue and fully explains the 2020 comment. Issue text is accurate and not stale; the 2024 maintainer position still holds.

*History:* always-repro'd -- identical on all 21 cached releases v1.4.1907 (2019-07-15, predating the issue) through v1.9.2607 (2026-07-29) and on main; -Fc has carried Flags<[DriverOption]> with no CoreOption since 6ee4074a4 (2016-12-28, first commit), per git log -L 505,505:include/dxc/Support/HLSLOptions.td. bisect deliberately NOT run: it drives each release's dxc.exe, the one caller that DOES handle -Fc, so it would score every release no-repro. See manual-case-release-history.txt.

*Labels:* add `api`, `up-for-grabs`.

*No Compiler Explorer link:* Compiler Explorer runs dxc.exe, the command-line driver -- which is the ONE caller that already handles -Fc (it parses with DxcFlags = CoreOption\|DriverOption). This issue is about IDxcCompiler/IDxcCompiler3::Compile, which parse with CompilerFlags = CoreOption alone; CE cannot call the compile API at all. A link would therefore demonstrate the opposite of the finding. The equivalent contrast is captured locally instead, in manual-case-cmdline-vs-api.txt (dxc.exe writes repro-fc.asm, 4103 bytes; the API answers E_INVALIDARG and writes nothing), and the API side is measured across 21 releases in manual-case-release-history.txt.

**[#2792](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/2792) — Need to report error when use constant which has offset bigger than root constant size.**  
<sub>batch 006 · triaged against `13730886e` · drafted by `claude-opus-4.6 (GitHub Copilot CLI)` · reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol`</sub>

No DXC has ever checked a cbuffer's size against its root constant block's num32BitConstants. RootConstants(b0, num32BitConstants = 1) with a two-float cbuffer at b0 compiles clean, exit 0, no diagnostic, and codegens the out-of-bounds read (extractvalue %dx.types.CBufRet.f32 %2, 1). Setting num32BitConstants = 2, making the shader correct, produces byte-identical output and the same shader hash: the field is parsed, serialised and printed but read by no validator, and DxilRootSignatureValidator registers a root constant as a one-register CBV range without passing Num32BitValues at all. Adjacent checking does run (binding b1 against a b0 cbuffer is rejected with 'Shader CBV descriptor range ... is not fully bound in root signature'), so this is a gap in that check rather than its absence. That check, VerifyRootSignatureWithShaderPSV, works from PSV bind info which carries no size, so a container-validation fix needs a PSV format change while a front-end fix does not. hlsl_clang_trunk does not diagnose it either, but also accepts the b1/b0 mismatch, so it has no root-signature-vs-shader checking yet at all. A request for a diagnostic that has never existed, not a regression.

*History:* always-repro'd across v1.4.1907..v1.9.2607 (all 20 releases probed linearly, no invalid probes); v1.4.1907 is the oldest probeable release, so this predates the report

*Labels:* add `diagnostic`, `enhancement`, `check-in-clang`; remove `bug`.

**[#3092](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/3092) — [SPIR-V] Allow thread group size to be specified with specialization constants**  
<sub>batch 008 · triaged against `13730886e` · drafted by `claude-opus-4.6` · reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol (independent draft review, SKILL.md step 10, applied selectively at collation)`</sub>

Still absent on main (13730886e) and on all 19 catalog releases with SPIR-V CodeGen v1.5.2010..v1.9.2607: [numthreads] rejects a [[vk::constant_id]] spec constant, and hlsl_clang_trunk emits the same first diagnostic. static const is already accepted, so what is missing is a dimension not known at compile time. **[#3189](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/3189) — [SPIR-V] Descriptor bindings assigned before dead code elimination**  
<sub>batch 007 · triaged against `13730886e` · drafted by `claude-opus-4.5 (Copilot CLI)` · reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol (independent draft review, step 10)`</sub>

Reproduces exactly as filed on ground truth and on all 19 probeable releases (v1.5.2010..v1.9.2607); v1.4.1907 is invalid-probe (no SPIR-V codegen, confirmed by a flag-free control, since the primary capture was demoted only for an unknown flag). With the reporter reconstructed shift flags the used cbuffer c is decorated Binding 2 while the two unused cbuffers are fully DCE-eliminated; with no shift flags it is Binding 4, so the behaviour is not shift-specific. Source confirms decorateResourceBindings runs at SpirvEmitter.cpp:840, before spirv-opt at 972/988, and -O0 shows a=0 b=1 c=2 unchanged. DXIL mode compacts (c at cb0), as noted in the thread. Not a defect to fix: s-perron stated the design position in 2024 (default must not change; opt-in spirv-opt renumbering pass welcome), and DXC already ships -fspv-preserve-bindings which keeps unused resources rather than compacting them. Remaining actions are relabelling as an enhancement and two docs gaps in SPIR-V.rst: the behaviour itself, and -fspv-preserve-bindings, which is undocumented.

*Labels:* add `enhancement`, `up-for-grabs`, `docs`.

**[#3439](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/3439) — Better demangling for improved error messages**  
<sub>batch 012 · triaged against `13730886e` · drafted by `claude-opus-4.6` · reviewed by `Claude Sonnet independent review (batch-012 step-10; blind 3414)`</sub>

Reproduces verbatim on main and on all 20 stable releases v1.4.1907..v1.9.2607: 'error: External function used in non-library profile: \01?CallMeMaybe@@YAHM_N@Z'. The emitter (CGHLSLMSFinishCodeGen.cpp:3405) prints PrintEscapedString(f.getName()) with no demangling, even though hlsl::dxilutil::DemangleFunctionName has existed since 47958a941 (2018-02-12), four months before the diagnostic was added in 4ade2fccc (2018-06-20), and is already called from three other sites. Two further mangled messages reproduced (export-param check at CGHLSLMSFinishCodeGen.cpp:3233; linker kUndefFunction at DxilLinker.cpp:401, also 20/20 releases). Partial, not blanket: DXIL-validator errors naming a library entry point come out readable. Control: the same compiler names the same function correctly in a Sema diagnostic ('redefinition of CallMeMaybe'). Demangling would give the bare name only; llvm-beanz's suggestion to move the diagnostic to Sema is what yields a signature. Clang trunk exits 0 and emits no diagnostic at all for this input (control confirms its diagnostics do surface in that pane), so the rewrite has not solved it.

*Labels:* add `diagnostic`.

**[#3535](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/3535) — Retrieving reflection data for structs used in input signatures**  
<sub>batch 013 · triaged against `13730886e` · drafted by `GPT-5 (Copilot CLI)` · reviewed by `gemini-3.1-pro-preview`</sub>

Confirmed on main (13730886e). Two separate gaps, both measured. (1) API: D3D12_SIGNATURE_PARAMETER_DESC has one string, SemanticName; and the full ID3D12ShaderReflection vtable has only GetConstantBufferByIndex/ByName and GetVariableByName leading to an ID3D12ShaderReflectionType, so GetMemberTypeName is unreachable from a signature parameter in any version. (2) Data: the names are never emitted -- with -Qkeep_reflect_in_dxil the reflection type table annotates %struct.CbStruct's fields but has no entry for the input struct, whose type is not even in the module; the field-name/semantic pair exists only pre-lowering at -fcgl. A fix is therefore preserve-then-expose, not a descriptor addition. Verified against dxa -dumpreflection driving each of 20 stable releases' own dxcompiler.dll (v1.4.1907..v1.9.2607): zero releases report the names. aclysma's GetMemberTypeName comment is correct about the method but it is cbuffer-only, so it does not satisfy this issue; coopp's 'I do not see a way' is correct. FXC behaves identically and DxilContainerTest asserts DXC matches d3dcompiler, so this is the D3D reflection model, not a DXC omission. Names do survive under -Zi as DW_TAG_member debug info -- a workaround for a code generator that owns its compile step.

*History:* Never worked; nothing regressed. bisect --linear reports v1.4.1907 no-repro then repro from v1.5.2010, which is an ARTEFACT and must not be read as a regression: before v1.5.2010 reflection metadata was left in the DXIL part rather than moved to STAT, so v1.4.1907's disassembly still carries the input struct's field-name annotation and the stdout predicate does not fire. That release's reflection API returns nothing, exactly like every release since (manual-case-reflection-matrix.txt, 20 releases, fixed instrument + per-release dxcompiler.dll). 5 prereleases excluded by policy; v1.2.0-alpha has no usable asset.

*Labels:* add `reflection`, `enhancement`, `api`.

**[#3927](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/3927) — [SPIR-V] Not all unnecessary bindings are eliminated using SPIR-V backend**  
<sub>batch 011 · triaged against `13730886e` · drafted by `GitHub Copilot CLI (claude-opus-4.6)` · reviewed by `claude-sonnet-5 (batch-011 independent draft review, applied selectively at collation)`</sub>

Still reproduces on main and all 19 SPIR-V-capable stable releases. The v1.6.2106 capture matches the reporter's 64-line module exactly. Tex0/SS0 keep DescriptorSet/Binding decorations because their sample feeds a branch whose two targets both end in OpKill; Tex1/SS1 are eliminated. At -O0 all four survive, showing that the observed elimination comes from spirv-opt rather than the emitter, consistent with the maintainer comment placing a fix there. The module is correct but not minimal, so this is an accepted optimization enhancement rather than a correctness bug.

*History:* always-repro'd across the 19 SPIR-V-capable stable releases v1.5.2010..v1.9.2607; v1.4.1907 is unprobeable because its package has no SPIR-V backend

*Labels:* add `enhancement`, `up-for-grabs`.

**[#4256](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/4256) — DXIL validation should run ComputeViewIdState pass**  
<sub>batch 014 · triaged against `13730886e` · drafted by `claude-opus-4.5` · reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol (independent draft review, step 10)`</sub>

Accurate and unaddressed. createComputeViewIdStatePass() is called only from the compile pipeline (PassManagerBuilder.cpp:391,709) and the linker (DxilLinker.cpp:1293), never from lib/DxilValidation/, so validation has no recomputed state to compare against. Measured with dxv over hand-edited modules from a vs_6_1 shader reading SV_ViewID: deleting dx.viewIdState, zeroing its dependency words, and replacing them with a deliberately false mapping all report 'Validation succeeded.' on main (1.9.0.5433, 13730886e) and on all six releases that ship dxv (v1.8.2502 through v1.9.2607), while an out-of-range storeOutput sig id and a vs_6_0 downgrade are rejected everywhere - so the validator does read the dx.op.viewID call, it just never checks it against the state. PR #6859 (2024) added PSVContentVerifier::VerifyViewIDDependence, which compares the PSV0 part with DM.GetSerializedViewIdState() (two copies of the same producer-supplied metadata) and returns early when the module state is empty and PSV is all zero, so it does not close the gap. Enhancement, not a bug: nothing DXC emits is wrong and nothing regressed; the exposure is to third-party DXIL producers and to drivers that trust the state.

*Labels:* add `enhancement`, `validation`.

*No Compiler Explorer link:* The symptom is not visible in a Compiler Explorer pane. It lives in dxv/IDxcValidator run over a DXIL module that DXC did not produce -- the modules are hand-edited (dx.viewIdState deleted, zeroed, or falsified), and CE compiles HLSL with dxc and shows the resulting DXIL. It has no way to feed a doctored module back into the validator, and repro.hlsl on its own compiles cleanly on every DXC (that is the control, variant-control-dxc-pipeline). A CE link would show a clean compile and be read as no-repro.

**[#4341](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/4341) — [HLSL 2021] Setter array subscript operator overload**  
<sub>batch 015 · triaged against `13730886e` · drafted by `claude-opus-5` · reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol (independent draft review, step 10)`</sub>

Writing through a user-defined operator[] is still rejected (error: expression is not assignable), on main (13730886e) and on all 16 stable releases from v1.6.2112 through v1.9.2607; the four older releases predate HLSL 2021 and are not evidence. The repro seeds a known value and writes a different one, so a landed write and a discarded write are distinguishable: neither predicate ever changed, so this has always been a diagnostic and never a silent miscompile. Both explanations in the thread still hold - references are unsupported (Sema::BuildReferenceType), and a trailing const is not part of a member function signature, so a const/non-const operator[] pair is a redeclaration. clang trunk on Compiler Explorer emits the identical diagnostic, with a control pane proving it is not an artefact of incomplete HLSL support.

*Labels:* add `enhancement`, `hlsl2021`.

**[#4501](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/4501) — [SPIR-V] Debug info should use DebugBuildIdentifier and DebugStoragePath with -Fd flag**  
<sub>batch 015 · triaged against `13730886e` · drafted by `claude-opus-5` · reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol (independent draft review, step 10)`</sub>

Feature request, never implemented: no emitter for DebugBuildIdentifier or DebugStoragePath exists anywhere in the DXC tree, and none of the 16 stable releases that can emit NonSemantic.Shader.DebugInfo.100 (v1.6.2112 onward) produces either. The premise has also shifted: -Fd is rejected with -spirv since v1.7.2207 (e80724a7a, 17 days after filing), and on v1.6.2112 it failed with "Unable to find required part in blob", so no -Fd path for SPIR-V has ever existed to extend.

*Labels:* add `enhancement`, `debug info`.

**[#4615](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/4615) — DXIL debug locations do not respect #line directives**  
<sub>batch 016 · triaged against `13730886e` · drafted by `claude-opus-5` · reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol`</sub>

Reproduces on main (1.9.0.5433, public commit 13730886e) and on 19 of 20 stable releases: DXIL !DILocation/!DIFile carry the physical line and file for code after a #line directive. It is deliberate -- PR #2991 passes UseLineDirectives=false at four CGDebugInfo getPresumedLoc sites and shipped a test asserting it; adam-yang said so in-thread in 2022 and the reporter accepted the default, narrowing the ask to an opt-in flag. That flag does not exist: the only #line compile option is -ignore-line-directives, which moves the opposite way (it makes even diagnostics report the physical location), and -line-directive is rewriter-only. Measured contrast in one build on one source: diagnostics report virtual-source.hlsl:400:17 and -spirv -fspv-debug=line emits OpLine 400 against OpString virtual-source.hlsl, so only DXIL debug info uses the physical location; hlsl_clang_trunk on Compiler Explorer already emits !DILocation(line: 400) with !DIFile(filename: "virtual-source.hlsl"). The live item is therefore an enhancement (an opt-in flag), and whether to add it is a maintainer decision this triage does not pre-empt.

*Labels:* add `debug info`, `enhancement`.

**[#4721](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/4721) — Support applying clang fix-its automatically**  
<sub>batch 017 · triaged against `13730886e` · drafted by `claude-opus-5` · reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol`</sub>

Feature request, still open and still accurate, but narrower than the title: dxc already computes and prints clang fix-it hints and cannot apply them. All 20 stable releases v1.4.1907-v1.9.2607 reject -fixit, -fixit=, -fixit-recompile and -Xclang; /fixit only 'succeeds' because unrecognised /-flags are silently dropped (byte-identical object). The machinery is present and already linked into dxcompiler (FixItRewriter.cpp, ExecuteCompilerInvocation.cpp:53, CC1Options.td:396); the gap is HLSLOptions.td, which declares no fixit and no Xclang, so no driver path selects FixItAction. llvm-project's HLSL clang runs the same rewriter today via -Xclang -fixit ('FIX-IT applied suggested code changes'), with a control proving the flag causes it. Ask 3 is worse than unimplemented: dxr prints the hint, exits 0 and silently drops the diagnosed initializer.

*Labels:* add `enhancement`, `diagnostic`, `rewriter`.

**[#6727](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/6727) — Support IMul/UMul/UDiv with two outputs from HLSL**  
<sub>batch 011 · triaged against `13730886e` · drafted by `claude-opus-4.6 (GitHub Copilot CLI)` · reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol (worker independent review); claude-sonnet-5 (batch-011 final independent draft review, applied selectively)`</sub>

Feature request, still unimplemented: DXIL defines IMul=41, UMul=42 and UDiv=43 in op class BinaryWithTwoOuts, but no HLSL spelling reaches them -- gen_intrin_main.txt has no entry and the only in-tree emitter is the DXBC-to-DXIL converter. Written the only way HLSL allows, the high half of a 32x32 multiply costs a 64-bit widening and the optional 64-Bit integer feature, while quotient plus remainder remain separate udiv/urem. FXC emits one two-output DXBC udiv from the same source. All 20 stable releases compile the probe and none emits the DXIL op.

*History:* always-repro'd across all 20 stable releases v1.4.1907..v1.9.2607; no invalid probes

*Labels:* add `fxc-disagrees`.

**[#4273](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/4273) — How to remove unused cbuffer?**  
<sub>batch 014 · triaged against `13730886e` · drafted by `GitHub Copilot CLI (claude-opus-4.6)` · reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol (independent draft review, step 10)`</sub>

-remove-unused-globals never removes an explicit cbuffer block (nor an unused member inside one); only loose globals bound for $Globals are removal candidates. Reproduces on main 1.9.0.5433 (13730886e) via dxr.exe and on all 19 stable releases v1.5.2010..v1.9.2607 that can express the option; v1.4.1907 predates the rewriter option surface (invalid probe), so there is no regression. Structural in dxcrewriteunused.cpp, where HLSLBufferDecls go to a separate cbufferDecls list and are never added to unusedGlobals, and asserted by the lit test rewriter/remove-unused-globals.hlsl since 2020. tex3d answered the question in 2022 and converted the issue into an accepted feature request; it should stay open as an enhancement.

*No Compiler Explorer link:* The reported surface is the rewriter (dxr.exe / IDxcRewriter2::RewriteWithOptions). Compiler Explorer's DXC compilers run dxc.exe, which rejects -remove-unused-globals and -rewrite outright (variant-dxc-rejects-rewriter-flag-main-debug.txt), so CE cannot run this repro at all.

**[#2188](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/2188) — fxc.exe vs dxc.exe: "static const int" use as compile time constant**  
<sub>batch 004 · triaged against `eff900d5` · drafted by `claude-opus-5` · reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol`</sub>

Still fails on main (1.9.0.15422, eff900d54) and in all 20 releases v1.4.1907..v1.9.2607, with the reported two errors. Root cause is narrower than the title: a component read of a const vector is not a constant expression (a const scalar is), so both the groupshared array bound and the [numthreads] arguments fail from one cause. FXC 10.1 compiles all cases and folds to dcl_thread_group 8,8,1; clang-dxc shares the gap. Codified in DXC's own tests (const-expr.hlsl:379-382, attributes.hlsl:659) as 'fxc-pass' / expected-error.

> ⚠️ **Issue text is stale.** Title blames 'static const int'; static const scalars work. The trigger is reading a component of a const vector (c2Thread.x), which is narrower and differently worded.

*Labels:* add `type-system`, `hlsl-next`.

**[#2331](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/2331) — Problem with DXIL signing and switch case/enum use**  
<sub>batch 006 · triaged against `13730886e` · drafted by `claude-opus-4.6` · reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol`</sub>

Reproduces on main (1.9.0.5433, 13730886e) and on every release back to the v1.4.1907 floor: a switch over an enum class covering every enumerator with no default:, in a non-void function, lowers the fall-off-the-end path to an LLVM 'unreachable', which DXIL disallows, so validation fails with 'Instructions must be of an allowed type' (E_FAIL, not a crash). Signing is not implicated: validation fails, so nothing is signed, and the reporter's 'DXIL.dll not found' warning is environmental -- every release probed had a dxil.dll beside it, and current builds do not consult one. Two secondary body claims have gone stale (see text-stale). Maintainers' 2024 position is won't-fix-in-DXC / handled in Clang; clang trunk emits no unreachable for a cut-down form of the same construct.

> ⚠️ **Issue text is stale.** Body claims B1 and B2 are stale: commenting out one case no longer 'validates clean' and adding a fourth enumerator no longer reaches the validator -- both are now 'error: control may reach end of non-void function [-Wreturn-type]' at Sema, changed between v1.4.1907 and v1.5.2010. The main symptom and B3 (default: compiles clean) still hold.

*Labels:* add `validation`, `incorrect-code`.

**[#3055](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/3055) — Improve error reporting for intrinsic methods with type mismatched arguments**  
<sub>batch 005 · triaged against `13730886e` · drafted by `claude-sonnet-4.6 (GitHub Copilot CLI)` · reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol (independent draft review, step 10)`</sub>

Intrinsic-method overload resolution reports only argument-COUNT mismatches; the argument-TYPE mismatch note is elided, so tex.Sample(SamplerComparisonState, float2) lists only the 3/4/5-argument overloads and never mentions the sampler type. The 2-argument candidate the user meant is the one suppressed. Unchanged v1.4.1907..main. Source: MatchArguments computes badArgIdx (SemaHLSL.cpp:5396) and the caller discards it (11364-11369), returning a bare TDK_NonDeducedMismatch (11456) whose note SemaOverload.cpp:9355-9360 elides by an explicit HLSL Change. Not specific to Sample -- GatherRed is identical. FXC lists the candidate signatures showing SamplerState; hlsl_clang_trunk already emits 'no known conversion from SamplerComparisonState to hlsl::SamplerState for 1st argument'. Note the issue body was edited 2023-09-27, after the 2023-07-14 comment saying it compiles.

> ⚠️ **Issue text is stale.** Not the title or body -- the thread. llvm-beanz commented 2023-07-14 'This compiles successfully now', and the body was then edited 2023-09-27, so the correction sits above the report it appears to correct. A reader going top-down concludes the issue is fixed; it reproduces byte-identically from v1.4.1907 to main. The comment is about a DIFFERENT thing (the shader now compiles because a valid overload was substituted); the filed complaint is that the diagnostic never names the sampler-type mismatch, and that is unchanged.

*History:* always-repro'd (v1.4.1907..v1.9.2607, all 20 releases probed linearly; v1.4.1907 output byte-identical to main)

**[#3811](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/3811) — Reading uninitialized value in dynamic loop produces undef with no error/warning**  
<sub>batch 010 · triaged against `13730886e` · drafted by `Claude Sonnet 4.5 (GitHub Copilot CLI)` · reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol (SKILL.md step 10 initial and final-draft reviews, applied selectively at collation)`</sub>

The underlying validator gap still holds, but the exact repro is no longer silent. The loop version exits 0 with a -Wparameter-usage warning and its define void @main() is line-for-line identical (27/27) to the DXIL pasted in 2021: phi float [ %10, %5 ], [ undef, %4 ] feeding fadd, and undef reaching the output when count <= 0. DXIL validation accepts it. The straight-line spelling is still rejected by the validator (E_FAIL 0x80004005, InstrNoReadingUninitialized) on main and on both ends of the release range. The mechanism is one line of source: lib/DxilValidation/DxilValidation.cpp has bool LegalUndef = isa<PHINode>(&I), so the rule is local and syntactic and PHI nodes are exempt by name -- through the loop, fadd operand is the phi, not literally UndefValue. A local-variable restatement remains completely silent, proving the 2023 out-parameter warning did not close the validator hole. Not optimisation-dependent (-Od reproduces). Related to #3009, #3706, and #3693, but not a duplicate: those exercise direct undef arithmetic, resource indexing, and nested out-of-bounds Sema handling rather than PHI-carried propagation.

**[#8527](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/8527) — pragma once is case sensitive**  
<sub>batch 004 · triaged against `eff900d5` · drafted by `claude-opus-5 (Copilot CLI)` · reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol`</sub>

Reproduces on main (1.9.0.15422, eff900d54) and on every release v1.4.1907..v1.9.2607; not a regression. Title understates it: not case folding -- #pragma once is keyed on the path AS SPELLED, so './x.hlsli' vs 'x.hlsli' fails identically with the case held constant. DxcArgsFileSystemImpl::TryFindOrOpen matches includes by wcscmp on the spelled name and GetFileInformationByHandle reports the slot handle as the file index, so FileManager's UniqueID dedup sees two files. Matching-case control compiles clean; #ifndef guards are an effective workaround. Measured on Windows/NTFS only. No CE link: multi-file repro, and the single-file fold measures clang's pragma-once-in-main-file rule instead.

> ⚠️ **Issue text is stale.** Title says 'case sensitive'. Case is not the mechanism: #pragma once keys on the path as spelled, so './x' vs '././x' fails with case held constant. The real scope is wider than the title.

*No Compiler Explorer link:* no valid single-file demonstration exists. The repro needs a header plus two includers and CE is single-file; CE also runs Linux, where the reported case-mismatched name does not exist. The obvious fold -- a file including itself under a different spelling of its own path -- was built, run on CE and REJECTED: the identical construction with a matching spelling fails the same way, so it measures clang's documented 'pragma once is ignored in the main file' rule, not this defect. Evidence: manual-case-godbolt.txt, variant-selfinclude-samespelling-main-debug.txt.

**[#2530](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/2530) — Array bound with static const variable**  
<sub>batch 005 · triaged against `13730886e` · drafted by `claude-sonnet-4.6 (GitHub Copilot CLI)` · reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol (independent draft review, step 10)`</sub>

Both cases in the body still fail on main (13730886e). Case 1 fails on all 20 releases v1.4.1907..v1.9.2607 (linear scan); case 2 fails at both endpoints. FXC 10.1 compiles both. The bound is not an integer constant expression under the C++03 ICE rules DXC inherited from clang: CheckICE accepts an explicit cast only when its operand is a FloatingLiteral, so uint(<static const float>) is non-ICE, BuildArrayType makes a VariableArrayType and SemaType.cpp:2143 emits err_hlsl_vla. Case 2 is the same rule one level out via checkInitIsICE. float array[uint(1.0f)] and a static const uint bound both compile; dropping the cast instead gives err_array_size_non_int, a different path. clang's HLSL front end rejects both too, naming the constant-expression rule. Resolution is a language decision.

*Labels:* add `diagnostic`.

**[#3044](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/3044) — Feature request: option to preprocess without removing comments**  
<sub>batch 012 · triaged against `13730886e` · drafted by `GitHub Copilot CLI (claude-opus-4.6)` · reviewed by `Claude Sonnet independent review (batch-012 step-10; blind 3414)`</sub>

Never implemented: comments are dropped by -P on all 20 stable releases and main, and -C/-CC are rejected as Unknown argument. The capability is already in the library - PrintPreprocessedOutput honours ShowComments/ShowMacroComments and CompilerInvocation parses -C/-CC on the cc1 path - but dxcompilerobj.cpp builds PreprocessorOutputOptions by hand and hardcodes both to 0, and HLSLOptions.td has no C/CC entry. So this is option plumbing, not a new capability, matching pow2clk's 2020 assessment.

**[#3237](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/3237) — Library Reflection : Listing parameters return E_FAIL**  
<sub>batch 009 · triaged against `13730886e` · drafted by `claude-opus-4.6 (GitHub Copilot CLI)` · reviewed by `GPT (collation)`</sub>

Reproduces on main (13730886e) and on all 21 measured releases v1.4.1907..v1.9.2607: ID3D12FunctionParameterReflection::GetDesc returns E_FAIL and D3D12_FUNCTION_DESC.FunctionParameterCount reads 0 for an exported library function. CFunctionReflection::GetFunctionParameter ignores its index and returns an always-E_FAIL singleton, the count field is marked // Unset:, and RDAT RuntimeDataFunctionInfo carries no parameter records at all, so parameter reflection was never implemented rather than regressed; the stub is unchanged since c1b662784 (2018-04-11). Measured with a committed C++ harness driving each release's own dxcompiler.dll, because dxc.exe never calls this API and triage.py bisect cannot drive it.

*History:* always-repro'd across v1.4.1907..v1.9.2607 (21 releases, including the non-bisectable v1.5.2003, each driven through its OWN dxcompiler.dll by refl3237.exe; see manual-case-release-history.txt) plus main-debug. PARAM0-GETDESC=0x80004005 and FunctionParameterCount=0 in every row; no invalid probes. DO NOT run triage.py bisect on this issue: it resolves each tag to that release's dxc.exe, which never calls the reflection API, so it would score every release no-repro and report a confident never-repro'd-in-releases -- the exact opposite of the truth. It was deliberately not run. v1.4.1907 is the bisection floor and reproduces, and git log -S dates the stub to c1b662784 (2018-04-11), so the defect predates every probeable release and the 2020-11-03 report.

*Labels:* add `api`, `test`.

*No Compiler Explorer link:* Compiler Explorer runs dxc.exe only. The reported defect is the HRESULT returned by ID3D12FunctionParameterReflection::GetDesc, an API dxc.exe never calls, and CE cannot load dxcompiler.dll and drive IDxcContainerReflection. No dxc switch prints per-parameter reflection (-Fre writes the blob, -dumpbin dumps the container; neither calls GetFunctionParameter), so no CE pane could show the symptom. Measured instead with the committed refl3237 harness against 21 released dxcompiler.dll builds; see manual-case-release-history.txt.

**[#3259](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/3259) — Crash in TranslatePtrIfUsedByLoweredFn**  
<sub>batch 005 · triaged against `13730886e` · drafted by `claude-opus-4.6` · reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol (independent draft review, step 10)`</sub>

Still crashes on Debug main (13730886e): DXASSERT_NOMSG(Ty) at lib/DXIL/DxilUtil.cpp:877 in hlsl::dxilutil::WrapInArrayTypes, called from TranslatePtrIfUsedByLoweredFn (the frame in the title), exit 0x80000003. Root cause is unchanged from the reporter's 2020 diagnosis: GetLoweredUDT returns nullptr for a struct with an embedded object type (HLLowerUDT.cpp:67, and :72 for nested structs), ScalarReplAggregatesHLSL.cpp:426 does not check it, so the null reaches WrapInArrayTypes at :436. Not Debug-only: DXASSERT_NOMSG is a no-op under NDEBUG (Global.h:369) and the null type flows on to Builder.CreateAlloca at :450, so all 19 releases that support as_6_5 (v1.5.2010, released three weeks before this was filed, through v1.9.2607) access-violate reading address 0. v1.5.2010 crashes with empty stderr. Compiler Explorer's dxc_1_6_2112 and dxc_trunk both SIGSEGV. Any HLSL object type triggers it (SamplerState too) at any nesting depth; a uint payload compiles cleanly. Confined to DispatchMesh's payload operand -- IsPtrUsedByLoweredFn (ScalarReplAggregatesHLSL.cpp:310) has TraceRay/ReportHit/CallShader commented out under a TODO.

*History:* always-repro'd across v1.5.2010..v1.9.2607 (19 releases); v1.4.1907 predates as_6_5 and is an invalid probe. NOT an NDEBUG artefact -- the release builds crash too (0xC0000005, read of address 0), because only the assert is compiled out and the null type still reaches CreateAlloca

*Labels:* add `incorrect-code`.

**[#3429](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/3429) — DXC Validation Error: TGSM pointers must originate from an unambiguous TGSM global variable**  
<sub>batch 009 · triaged against `13730886e` · drafted by `claude-opus-4.5 (Copilot CLI)` · reviewed by `GPT (collation)`</sub>

Still fails on main (1.9.0.5433, 13730886e) and on all 20 bisectable releases v1.4.1907..v1.9.2607 -- probed linearly under two predicates, 42 probes, all exit 0x80004005, no invalid probes; none of the 20 measured release binaries compiled it, and v1.4.1907 (2019-07) is the floor. The merged pointer is not ambiguous: with -Vd the compile succeeds and both phi float addrspace(3)* have every incoming value GEPing the SAME global. lib/DxilValidation/DxilValidation.cpp (~L3820-3849) walks GEP/bitcast chains only when the instruction is itself a GEP or bitcast, so any other TGSM-pointer-typed instruction, phi included, is rejected without its operands being examined; dxv.exe built from this tree rejects the module too, so it is the in-tree validator and not only the redistributable dxil.dll. All five optimization levels were captured on main: -Od and -O0 compile clean, -O1, -O2 and -O3 all fail, so the reporter's workaround costs all optimization and not just -O3. At -O0 no phi of groupshared pointers is formed at all, which is why it escapes. CAUTION for anyone re-running this: v1.4.1907 emits the same rule with no "error: " prefix and an instruction address instead of a source line:column, and -O1/-O2 name the phis differently from -O3, so a predicate carrying the prefix or the instruction text scores reproducing probes as no-repro -- one such predicate faked a transition at v1.5.2010. Whether the walk should accept a merge whose operands all resolve to one global, or the optimizer should not form it, is a maintainer decision this triage does not make.

*History:* always-repro'd across v1.4.1907..v1.9.2607 (all 20 bisectable releases probed linearly under both predicates; no invalid probes). v1.4.1907 is the bisection floor, so this means 'for as long as it is checkable'. The 2021-02-04 report is nonetheless covered: v1.5.2010 (2020-10-22) predates it and reproduces. Not an NDEBUG artefact -- the symptom is a diagnostic from a Release-built validator, not an assert.

*Labels:* add `validation`.

**[#3708](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/3708) — Component swizzling / vector indexing not considered a constant expression**  
<sub>batch 010 · triaged against `13730886e` · drafted by `claude-opus-4.6` · reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol (SKILL.md step 10 initial and final-draft reviews, applied selectively at collation)`</sub>

Still reproduces on main (1.9.0.5433, 13730886e) and on all 20 measured releases v1.4.1907..v1.9.2607, no invalid probes; v1.6.2104 shipped 4 days before the report and reproduces. The body is narrower than the measured behavior: each tested integral-constant-expression use rejects a vector or matrix component, not just an array bound - case labels, enumerators, non-type template arguments and [numthreads] each fail with their own diagnostic. Also refused: .x on a static const scalar, matrix ._11/._m00/[0][0], .r, rvalue swizzles, v2[1], v2.x+v2.y. The tested scalar-alias workaround fails too, and constexpr is not a DXC keyword. Unaffected by -HV 2016/2017/2018/2021. FXC 10.1 accepts every tested form including case v2.x and vector<float,v2.y>; clang trunk accepts (10).x - the exact case filed - and rejects the static const ones only under the ordinary C++ non-constexpr rule, accepting them when spelled constexpr uint2. Rejected by two HLSL-specific sites in ExprConstant.cpp (CheckICE blacklist at 9035-9036, IntExprEvaluator::VisitCastExpr at 7749-7750), both dating to the 2016 initial commit; err_hlsl_vla is raised at SemaType.cpp:2142-2146. The only HLSLVectorElementExpr visitor in the constant evaluator is in VectorExprEvaluator, so only vector-result swizzles fold; there is no VisitExtMatrixElementExpr at all. DXC pins this in its own test suite - tools/clang/test/SemaHLSL/const-expr.hlsl:379-382, added 2017-08-29 in 6322c8ca3 (PR #605) - marking it fxc-pass with the comment "It would be desirable to have this supported", so any fix must update that test. Whether to fold component access into a constant expression is a language decision (match FXC, or adopt clang constexpr rules which HLSL cannot spell) and is not pre-empted here.

*History:* always-repro'd across v1.4.1907..v1.9.2607 (all 20 measured releases, no invalid probes)

*Labels:* add `hlsl-next`, `usability`.

**[#3726](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/3726) — Sema should not allow assignment to resource**  
<sub>batch 010 · triaged against `13730886e` · drafted by `claude-opus-4.6` · reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol (SKILL.md step 10 initial and final-draft reviews, applied selectively at collation)`</sub>

Reproduces on all 21 measured DXC builds, v1.4.1907..main (13730886e), exactly as filed. The front end is silent: -fcgl exits 0 with empty stderr on all 21 builds, and no resource-assignment diagnostic exists in DiagnosticSemaKinds.td (191 err_hlsl entries; the only resource-named one is about intrinsic arguments). The rejection comes from the DXIL back end -- DxilCondenseResources.cpp:699/701, reported from LegalizeResourceUseHelper inside DxilLowerCreateHandleForLib, ~150 passes after -dxilgen -- and its first line is a catch-all fallback telling a pixel shader with no library functions that "exported library functions cannot have resource parameters". -spirv exits 0 with no diagnostic on all 19 SPIR-V-capable measured releases; the emitted module binds x0/x1/x2 (the assignment targets) while r0/r1/r2 never appear. Because the issue asks for the as-filed source to be rejected, that is evidence of acceptance and lowering shape, not a miscompile. New: hlsl_clang_trunk also accepts it at exit 0 and lowers the store through r0 (controlled: the same shader minus the assignment compiles cleanly on both dxc_trunk and hlsl_clang_trunk). Scope matters and is a design question: with x0/x1/x2 static (as a 2024 comment suggests) or function-local (PR #3721 shape) the DXIL path also exits 0, so a blanket Sema rule would reject forms DXC accepts today. Reader trap: applying the "should be static" correction makes the DXIL half compile cleanly, which looks like cannot-reproduce. History: match.json (positive, the back-end error) always-repro'd across v1.4.1907..v1.9.2607; match-sema.json (INVERTED POLARITY -- a match would mean the front end diagnoses it, i.e. fixed) never-repro'd across v1.5.2010..v1.9.2607, v1.4.1907 demoted to invalid-probe by the SPIR-V feature marker on cmd.txt line 2 and re-probed separately (also silent).

*History:* always-repro'd across v1.4.1907..v1.9.2607 (match.json, the DXIL back-end error); front end never diagnosed it across v1.5.2010..v1.9.2607 (match-sema.json, inverted polarity, 1 release skipped as unprobeable)

*Labels:* add `diagnostic`, `check-in-clang`.

**[#3835](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/3835) — Internal compiler error on shader validation**  
<sub>batch 013 · triaged against `13730886e` · drafted by `claude-opus-4.5 (GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.79-2)` · reviewed by `gemini-3.1-pro-preview`</sub>

Crashes in clang CodeGen, not in DXIL validation despite the title. An incomplete array type initialised by array assignment (float x[] = s.arr) reaches EmitAutoVarAlloca uncompleted and trips assert(!isIncompleteType()) in isConstantSizeType; with asserts compiled out the same input null-derefs in ConvertScalarOrVector/AddMissingCastOpsInInitList, which is the reported access violation (proved by stepping past the asserts in the debug binary). Second shape: the 5-line minimal repro does not crash on release builds but silently emits an empty entry point on all 20 releases, and as a compute restatement produces undef UAV stores that DXC own validator rejects. FXC compiles the filed shader and generates correct code; Clang HLSL front end rejects it with array initializer must be an initializer list on exactly the crashing lines. Predicate is internal_failure keyed on exit status, not message: 0xE0000001 on the debug build, 0xC0000005 on releases, one of them empty-stderr, so any message-based predicate would invent a fix boundary.

*History:* always-repro'd across all 20 bisectable stable releases v1.4.1907..v1.9.2607 (linear sweep, no invalid probes); earliest reproduction predates the 2021-06 report by two years

Measured on CE: (1) with no #include, -H prints no trace at all, so the working case cannot be shown either; (2) a pane that #includes its own header gets "fatal error: file not found"; (3) -P additionally renders as <No output file>. **[#3872](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/3872) — SV_ShadingRate allowed in certain shader signatures where it shouldn't be allowed**  
<sub>batch 013 · triaged against `13730886e` · drafted by `GitHub Copilot CLI (claude-opus-4.5)` · reviewed by `gemini-3.1-pro-preview`</sub>

Confirmed on main at 13730886e and on every stable release back to v1.4.1907. All four SemanticInterpretation cells the reporter names (HSCPIn, HSCPOut, DSCPIn, DSOut) still accept SV_ShadingRate and emit it as a real system value; the D3D12 VRS spec permits setting it only from VS, GS or MS and rules out DS by name, so the report is correct. Controls show DXC does have the diagnostic and reaches it in hs and ds for NA cells, so the silence is a table decision rather than an unreached check. The DXIL validator does not catch it either and structurally cannot: ValidationRule::SmSemantic reads the same SigPoint::GetInterpretation table (measured with dxv plus a root-signature positive control). The fix is one CSV row in utils/hct/hctdb.py:8019 since the .inl is generated; it is source-breaking, so it likely wants a release note. GSVIn, which the reporter raised as a question rather than a claim, is also still accepted and still needs a spec answer. Clang trunk does not model the semantic at all (unknown HLSL semantic), so these cells remain an open input to the clang semantic work; FXC rejects it everywhere including the spec-legal VS position because it predates SM 6.4, so it is not evidence.

*History:* always-repro'd across v1.4.1907..v1.9.2607 (20 stable releases, probed linearly with match-portable.json). match.json first scored v1.4.1907 no-repro; the clause matrix shows only the disassembler-spelling clauses flipped (the 2019 disassembler prints NONE in the SysValue column where trunk prints SHDINGRATE) while every acceptance clause held, and the DXIL signature-element metadata carrying system-value kind 29 is identical in both, so that transition is an instrument artefact and not a behaviour change. The four disputed table cells are unchanged since ecb4e3b4b (2018-10-22) introduced the semantic, which predates every probeable release.

*Labels:* add `diagnostic`, `incorrect-code`.

**[#3943](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/3943) — #pragma once cannot support path aliases**  
<sub>batch 011 · triaged against `13730886e` · drafted by `claude-opus-4.5` · reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol (independent draft review, step 10)`</sub>

Reproduces on main (1.9.0.5433, 13730886e) and on all 20 stable releases v1.4.1907..v1.9.2607. #pragma once identity is a wcscmp of the requested path string, not file identity: -I vs source-relative, .., and case (on case-insensitive NTFS) all alias, while two spellings that normalise to one string dedupe. dxcfilesystem.cpp sets the Windows file index to the handle value, so every distinct spelling gets its own FileEntry.

*No Compiler Explorer link:* Measured infeasible, not assumed (manual-case-ce-infeasible.txt, dxc_trunk + dxc_1_6_2112). The single-file fold -- a pane that includes itself under two spellings -- is not a restatement: its known-good CONTROL with MATCHED spellings fails identically, and dxc itself says why (warning: #pragma once in main file). CE also cannot resolve its own pane by name ('<source>' file not found), so no fold runs at all.

**[#4206](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/4206) — Incorrect 'D3D_SVF_USED' flag with fields in $Globals_cbuffer**  
<sub>batch 014 · triaged against `13730886e` · drafted by `GitHub Copilot CLI (claude-opus-4.6)` · reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol (independent draft review, step 10)`</sub>

Reproduces on main (1.9.0.5433, 13730886e), and worse than reported. dxa -dumpreflection on the container gives the reported false positive AND an unreported false negative: SkyLightColor (never read) is reported (D3D_SVF_USED), while WorldPosToProbeCoord (read twice, and the array the bad index belongs to) is reported uFlags 0; ProbeCoordToWorldPos is correct and serves as the per-run instrument self-test. Removing the single "- 1" from the index makes all three flags correct (U,U,0) with the $Globals layout unchanged, so the negative index is the trigger, exactly as reported. Root cause confirmed by source reading and matches the reporter: GetCBOffset (DxilCondenseResources.cpp:2566) folds add i32 %ProbeIndex, -1 to unsigned 0xFFFFFFFF, the caller shifts to 0xFFFFFFF0, and MarkCBUse (:2605) does upper_bound(offset) -> end() then it-- , landing on the LAST field; the same fold is why the intended field at offset 0 is never marked. One mis-folded offset, two wrong answers in opposite directions -- a fix must address both. Symptom is invisible to dxc.exe (which never calls ID3D12ShaderReflection) and to -Fc disassembly (the used bit is kDxilFieldAnnotationCBUsedTag in the STAT reflection module), so it was measured through a harness-as-compiler that compiles with dxc and reads back with dxa -dumpreflection.

*History:* Two faces, two histories, measured over all 20 stable releases v1.4.1907..v1.9.2607 (manual-case-release-history.txt: two subjects x two reader columns -- fixed ground-truth reader, and each release paired with its OWN dxcompiler.dll; the columns agree on every row). match-falsenegative.json (WorldPosToProbeCoord, genuinely read, reported NOT used): always-repro'd, all 20 releases including v1.4.1907. match.json (SkyLightColor, never read, reported USED -- the reported symptom): no-repro on v1.4.1907 (2019-07-15), repro on v1.5.2010 (2020-10-22) and all 18 releases since, plus main. So the reported face regressed inside a ~15-month window. NOT the batch-013 metadata-relocation artefact: on v1.4.1907 the dump lists all three variables, the instrument self-test clause holds, and control-noneg scores fully correct there. NO commit is named: git merge-base --is-ancestor 4234a9ae5 v1.4.1907 SUCCEEDS and the tag tree already contains MarkCBUse, yet the shipped binary behaves as though it does not -- the v1.4.1907 tag tip is dated 2019-08-30, after the July 1907 release, so the tag is not a proxy for the shipped artifact. Compiling on main with -validator-version 1.4 does NOT restore the old answer (variant-valver14, run with --expect no-match, came back repro), so the transition is not merely the validator-version gate at DxilContainerReflection.cpp:2313. triage.py bisect deliberately NOT run: it substitutes each release dxc.exe for the registered harness, which would stop all reflection output and report a confident never-repro'd-in-releases.

*Labels:* add `bug`, `correctness`.

*No Compiler Explorer link:* Not reproducible on Compiler Explorer: the symptom lives in the container reflection (D3D_SVF_USED via ID3D12ShaderReflection / the STAT part), and CE's DXC panes show -Fc disassembly of the DXIL part only, which does not carry kDxilFieldAnnotationCBUsedTag. Verified locally: -Fc output for this shader has no cbuffer field annotations at all (scratch check), and dxa -extractpart=STAT yields a DxilProgramHeader that plain dxa cannot disassemble. Reading it needs dxa -dumpreflection, which CE does not run.

**[#4351](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/4351) — Rewriter incorrectly removes types that are used in a member array of another struct**  
<sub>batch 015 · triaged against `13730886e` · drafted by `claude-opus-5` · reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol (independent draft review, step 10)`</sub>

dxr -E InitArgs -remove-unused-globals deletes struct Child even though struct Parent declares Child MultipleChildren[2]; the emitted source then fails to compile with "unknown type name Child". Reproduces on main 1.9.0.5433 (13730886e) and on all 19 stable releases v1.5.2010..v1.9.2607 that can express the option; v1.4.1907 has no rewriter options at all (invalid probe), so there is no regression window. The non-array form Child SingleChild is unaffected, and the rewriter own accounting under -no-warnings confirms the decision: //found 1 types to remove vs //found 0. The 2022-08-15 comment about unused function parameters also reproduces (agent-constructed shader). One root cause in dxcrewriteunused.cpp: type liveness is computed from value references only, so fieldDecl->getType()->getAsTagDecl() returns null for an array member and FunctionDecl::params() is never visited. Real, unfixed, no linked PR; keep open and add the rewriter label.

*Labels:* add `rewriter`.

*No Compiler Explorer link:* Compiler Explorer runs the dxc driver, which cannot reach the rewriter at all: dxc rejects -remove-unused-globals with 'Unknown argument' (measured, variant-dxc-rejects-rewriter-flag-main-debug.txt), and CE ships no dxr. A pane could only show the rewriter's already-broken OUTPUT failing on an undefined type, which demonstrates nothing a reader could not guess and hides that DXC itself produced that source. Clang has no HLSL rewriter either, so a Clang pane adds nothing.

<sub>batch 016 · triaged against `13730886e` · drafted by `claude-opus-5` · reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol`</sub>

**[#4648](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/4648) — unsigned int{16,32,64}_t at global scope causes Segfault (attempted to read from 0x8)**  
<sub>batch 017 · triaged against `13730886e` · drafted by `claude-opus-5` · reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol`</sub>

Reproduces on main (13730886e) and on all 20 stable releases v1.4.1907..v1.9.2607; access violation reading 0x8, matching the reported message byte-for-byte from v1.6.2104 on (the two oldest releases crash with empty stderr, so a text predicate would falsely score them clean). ApplyTypeSpecSignToParsedType returns m_scalarTypes[newScalarType] (SemaHLSL.cpp:11233), which is null unless the source already named that type, since only six scalar slots are pre-populated and the rest are created lazily by LookupScalarTypeDef; naming uint16_t earlier makes the identical declaration compile. Wider than the title: also crashes as a local, parameter and struct member, and for any user typedef (typedef int MyInt; unsigned MyInt g;) with no 16-bit type or flags involved. Vector/matrix shorthands escape because they prime the scalar typedef, which is why the only in-tree test covers unsigned int64_t2 and not unsigned int64_t. Clang-HLSL already rejects the construct.
