**[#4701](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/4701) — DXC not optimizing out code related to groupshared**  
<sub>batch 017 · triaged against `13730886e` · drafted by `claude-opus-5` · reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol`</sub>

Reproduces on main (13730886e), byte-for-byte the IR quoted in 2022: the write-only groupshared array keeps both its addrspace(3) allocation and its store. Holds at the default level (-O3 per dxc --help) and at -O1/-Od. Measured two-sided: the identical dead array declared static, or function-local, is removed completely on all 20 catalogued stable releases v1.4.1907..v1.9.2607 and on main, while the groupshared arm survives on all 21 - so this is a persistent groupshared-specific gap, not a regression and not a recent improvement in the comparison case. Consequence is not cosmetic: at 64 KB the same never-read array fails DXIL validation (Total Thread Group Shared Memory used by main is 65536, exceeding maximum: 32768) where the static twin compiles to an empty main. FXC removes it entirely (no dcl_tgsm, ~1 instruction slot); the clang-based HLSL front end currently keeps it, so check-in-clang is already answered. Root cause: -fcgl shows groupshared emitted as external addrspace(3) global with no initializer vs internal global zeroinitializer for static; GlobalOpt bails at GlobalOpt.cpp:1707 (!hasLocalLinkage) and :1720 (!hasInitializer), and LowerStaticGlobalIntoAlloca requires IsStaticGlobal = internal linkage AND default address space (DxilUtil.cpp:114-117), excluding addrspace 3 by construction; no TGSM-specific pass covers the gap. A real fix needs module-wide liveness, since a TGSM store is dead only if no load exists anywhere. Not measured: any runtime/occupancy effect (no GPU). Whether the TGSM budget check should run after such an optimisation is a design decision, presented neutrally.

*Labels:* add `fxc-disagrees`.

**[#4722](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/4722) — `column_major` and `row_major` don't apply correctly to template-dependent types**  
<sub>batch 017 · triaged against `13730886e` · drafted by `claude-opus-5` · reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol`</sub>

Matrix orientation never reaches a template-dependent matrix type. #pragma pack_matrix(row_major) on a matrix<T,X,Y> member is silently dropped -- the row_major, column_major and no-pragma builds are byte-identical, while the same three without the template differ -- and an explicitly written row_major on such a member is instead rejected with 'can only be used with a matrix type' at template definition time, which is the issue's own test case. Both faces come from testing matrix-ness on a still-dependent type (SemaType.cpp:4359 skips, SemaType.cpp:5820 rejects). -Zpr does work on template-dependent members, because it takes the codegen-default route rather than annotating the type. Reproduces on all 16 stable releases that can compile HLSL 2021 templates, from v1.6.2112 to main.

*Labels:* add `bug`, `correctness`, `type-system`.

**[#4723](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/4723) — Support -M depfile generation flags during -P preprocess to file**  
<sub>batch 017 · triaged against `13730886e` · drafted by `claude-opus-5` · reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol`</sub>

Reproduces, and the mechanism is worse than the report suggests: under -P the -M family writes no depfile AND appends the dependency list to the preprocessed -Fi output, so the .i no longer compiles (E_FAIL, 'unknown type name'). Silent -- exit 0, no diagnostic, though dxc does warn for -Fo under -P. Two causes: DxcContext::Preprocess() never reaches ActOnBlob() where depfiles are written, and DxcCompilerObj::Compile writes the preprocessed text and the dependency rule to the same outStream. Identical on every release from v1.7.2207 (current when filed) to today. Not an enhancement: both flags work independently, only the combination is broken, and it corrupts a requested output.

*Labels:* add `diagnostic`.

*No Compiler Explorer link:* The observable is a set of FILES the driver writes (a .d depfile) and the contents of a -Fi preprocessed output; Compiler Explorer shows only the compiled result of a single translation unit, so it cannot display either. The repro is also multi-file by construction -- a dependency list is only meaningful with #include, and this one uses two nested headers -- and CE is single-file. A link would show a compile that is not the thing under test.

<sub>batch 006 · triaged against `13730886e` · drafted by `claude-opus-5` · reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol`</sub>

Still asserts on Debug main (13730886e): DXASSERT(0, 'not implemented yet') at lib/HLSL/HLOperationLower.cpp:8801 in TranslateCBAddressUserLegacy, exit 0x80000003. <sub>batch 012 · triaged against `13730886e` · drafted by `claude-opus-4.6 (GitHub Copilot CLI)` · reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol (independent draft review, step 10)`</sub>

**[#4415](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/4415) — Validator needs to prevent invalid handle in AnnotateHandle**  
<sub>batch 015 · triaged against `13730886e` · drafted by `claude-opus-5` · reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol (independent draft review, step 10)`</sub>

Both asks reproduce on main (1.9.0.5433, 13730886e). The front end still only warns (-Wuninitialized, exit 0), and DXIL validation still accepts dx.op.annotateHandle with a zeroinitializer/undef handle -- DXC own output, plus modules DXC never emitted, plus Microsoft signed dxil.dll from the v1.8.2505.1 archive. The decisive control: the same operand value on textureLoad is rejected by name ("Instructions should not read uninitialized value."), and corrupting the same annotateHandle props operand is also rejected, so the instruction is inspected but its handle operand never is. Source agrees: ValidateHandleArgs() routes AnnotateHandle, AnnotateNodeHandle, AnnotateNodeRecordHandle and CreateHandleForLib to break under "TODO: add custom validation for these intrinsics" while every other opcode reaches ValidateHandleArgsForInstruction(); that check landed in 9468120e6 (PR #5399, 2023-07-21), a year after this issue, and excluded AnnotateHandle from the start.

*History:* always-repro'd since SM 6.6 shipped: repro on all 16 stable releases from v1.6.2112 (2021-12-08) to v1.9.2607, and the doctored module is accepted by the dxv.exe of all 6 releases that ship one (v1.8.2502 onward). v1.4.1907 and v1.5.2010 are invalid-probe (no vs_6_6). bisect reports non-monotonic because v1.6.2104/v1.6.2106 are no-repro, but those SM 6.6 preview builds lower ResourceDescriptorHeap to createHandleForLib and are rejected by "opcode CreateHandleForLib should only be used in Library" -- an unrelated rule, not an invalid-handle check that later regressed.

**[#4492](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/4492) — [DXIL] Broken codegen for loading elements from FP16 matrix types in StructuredBuffer**  
<sub>batch 015 · triaged against `13730886e` · drafted by `claude-opus-5` · reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol (independent draft review, step 10)`</sub>

Structured-buffer 16-bit matrix element access uses a 4-byte scalar stride instead of 2. TranslateStructBufMatSubscript scales the element index by GetEltTypeByteSizeForConstBuf (the cbuffer 4-byte rule) while the same instruction's alignment operand uses the real 2-byte alloc size. Every offset is exactly double: the reporter's 16 loads span 62 bytes of a 32-byte element. Affects stores identically, writing 28 bytes past the element into the next one. Not a packing bug (doubled in both row- and column-major). Compiles and validates clean. Clang emits correct offsets.

*History:* Reproduces on every checkable release. The reporter's shader is clean on v1.4.1907/v1.5.2010 and broken from v1.6.2104 on, but that is a shader-shape boundary, not the defect's: those two releases vectorise the whole 32-byte struct load and never reach the per-element matrix path. Reduced to the issue body's own snippet it reproduces on v1.4.1907 too, the oldest release available, so the bug predates every checkable build. Both implicated functions date to the repo's first commit (6ee4074a4).

**[#4514](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/4514) — Variable inside a namespace not found**  
<sub>batch 016 · triaged against `13730886e` · drafted by `claude-opus-5` · reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol`</sub>

Reproduces on main (1.9.0.5433, 13730886e) and on all 20 stable releases v1.4.1907..v1.9.2607, probed linearly with no invalid probes; v1.4.1907 stderr is byte-identical to main, and the responsible line dates to the repository first commit 6ee4074a4 (2016-12-28), so the defect predates the bisection floor and the 2022 report. Diagnostic-quality issue: match.json quotes the reported error verbatim so classify() does not demote every reproducing release on its own no-member-named marker; no capture carries an invalid-probe-reason header. -HV is inert -- 2016/2017/2018/2021 all reproduce identically to no flag -- so cmd.txt correctly carries none and no fake version floor was introduced. Cause: HLSLBufferDecl::Create hardcodes the semantic DeclContext of every cbuffer/tbuffer to the TranslationUnitDecl (SemaHLSL.cpp:15420), so the namespace is only the lexical parent and the buffer members, republished through the transparent context, land in the TU; corroborated by -ast-dump and by debug info giving testVariable scope !0 and mangling ?testVariable@testBuffer@@3IB while a sibling namespace declaration gets DINamespace. The reporters Texture2D workaround is incidental and position-dependent: any namespace-scope declaration placed BEFORE the use works (static uint, struct), a second cbuffer does not, and moving it after main() re-breaks it -- four predictions written into the control shaders before running, all held. tbuffer identical. Compiler Explorer shows hlsl_clang_trunk behaving inversely to DXC, accepting the qualified name and rejecting the unqualified one, with its own control pane.

**[#4540](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/4540) — [DXIL] Incorrect codegen when using "static" on groupshared variables**  
<sub>batch 016 · triaged against `13730886e` · drafted by `claude-opus-5` · reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol`</sub>

Reproduces on main (1.9.0.5433) and on all 20 stable releases from v1.4.1907 to v1.9.2607, so it predates the 2022 report. `static groupshared uint` lowers to `@storeTile = internal unnamed_addr addrspace(3) global i1 false`; docs/DXIL.rst:240 defines i1 memory accesses for thread-local memory only, and i32/f32/f64 for groupshared. Removing the single token `static` gives `addrspace(3) global i32` -- that is the known-good control, and across 22 builds (20 stable releases, 1 prerelease, main) the repro emits i1 on 22/22 while the control emits it on 0/22, with the predicate self-test passing 22/22. Confirms the maintainer comment about the validator and the spec contradicting each other: DXIL validation accepts the i1 module on 22/22 builds, while a 64KB-groupshared control is correctly rejected on 22/22, so the validator does police groupshared memory and still does not object. Attributed by measurement with dxopt (null-pass control emits i32): -globalopt is necessary and sufficient, matching TryToShrinkGlobalToBoolean (lib/Transforms/IPO/GlobalOpt.cpp:1595); `static` supplies the internal linkage that makes the global eligible. The shrink is value-preserving per thread (loads come back as select/zext); what it breaks is the groupshared object type. Clang trunk emits addrspace(3) global i32 for the same source at -O3. The reporter's GPU-level symptom was not verified -- it needs hardware.


## Provenance and limits

- Ground truth is a **Debug** build of `main` (5 commits across batches). Debug matters: many older issues are asserts, which a Release build compiles out.
- **The release bisection floor is v1.4.1907** (2019-07), the oldest release shipping a usable `dxc`. For issues filed before it, "always reproduced" means "for as long as it is possible to check". SPIR-V issues have a higher floor still.
- **Compiler Explorer runs Release builds**, so a Debug-only assert looks clean there. CE corroborates the local build; it never overrules it. `dxc_trunk` is a rolling build and is not reproducible over time.
- **Sampling is deliberately unrepresentative.** Batches over-weight the oldest issues, so the verdict distribution here does not generalise to the backlog.
